paragraphs: One-sentence assessment | This career is worth exploring further only if you are willing to maintain long-term watch in a facility's main control room, follow procedures for parameter monitoring, control operations and records, determine causes before responding to abnormalities as expected, and accept operator licensing and facility training constraints. Attraction to the words "nuclear power plant" or "high pay" alone is insufficient.

Core output | Connect operating parameter records, periodic test results, control actions and responses, abnormalities and corrective measures, maintenance isolations and permits, and emergency response records into a traceable operating file: reviewable operating logs, test records and deviation reports, rather than merely stating that operation is normal.

20—120-minute safe trial | Conduct an off-site exercise with fictional main control room parameter trends, including power, coolant temperature and flow, and rod position. For 4 fictional parameter changes, write expected responses, procedural steps to check and three stop conditions requiring immediate supervisor reporting, then draft a one-sentence three-way communication following reading—judgment—report—action—review. Use only fictional data. Do not use this for real reactor control, operate any control system or bypass facility training.

First hurdle | Verify authorization boundaries first: who may operate main control room systems, approve equipment isolation and maintenance, and decide power reductions or reactor shutdown during abnormalities. NRC licenses personnel who operate or supervise control of commercial nuclear power reactors in the United States. Chinese civilian nuclear facility operators must hold Operator Licenses or Senior Operator Licenses. Nuclear power plant operators require associate-level education or higher and successful training and assessments. Licenses are valid for five years and require timely renewal applications.

Power operators (O*NET-SOC 51-8011.00, Nuclear Power Reactor Operators) operate or control nuclear reactors from nuclear power plant main control rooms. They follow policies and procedures to protect workers from radiation and ensure environmental safety; adjust control rod positions under standard procedures to regulate reactivity, reactor period, coolant temperature or power change rates; monitor all plant systems and examine instrument readings to assess output or effects on other equipment; record operating data such as surveillance test results and execute startup and shutdown procedures; diagnose system or unit abnormalities and recommend or take corrective action; implement lockout, tagging and isolation for safe maintenance; direct operators under emergency procedures when needed; and supervise technicians' procedural work.

entries: Reactor operation and control | Operate nuclear power reactors under policies and procedures, adjusting control rods to regulate reactivity, reactor period, coolant temperature or power change rates.

Parameter monitoring and data records | Monitor normal operation of all systems, examine instrument readings, record operating data such as surveillance test results, and identify and report equipment, instrument or control malfunctions.

Abnormality diagnosis and correction | Diagnose causes of system or unit abnormalities, recommend or take corrective actions, and authorize correction of identified operating inefficiencies or hazards.
Maintenance support and permits | Implement lockout, tagging and isolation for safe maintenance, and authorize unit repairs or changes in equipment and system operating status.
Emergencies and direction | Direct operators under emergency operating procedures and authorize operating status changes to control abnormalities.
Procedures and documents | Execute operating procedures such as startup and shutdown, and review and revise standard operating procedures.

Radiation and sampling supervision | Supervise technicians following procedures that protect workers and the environment, and direct collection and testing of air, water, gas or solid samples and measurement of radiation intensity or type in work areas.

paragraphs: Work takes place almost entirely inside nuclear power plant main control rooms. O*NET shows 100% daily face-to-face discussions, 99% daily controlled indoor work, 97% daily telephone use and 88% daily email use. Teamwork is extremely important to 89%, and 69% maintain constant contact with others.

Responsibility and pressure are routine: O*NET shows 91% rating accuracy extremely important, 82% reporting extremely serious error consequences, 66% holding extremely high responsibility for others' health and safety, and 72% reporting decisions as very important to coworkers' or organizational outcomes. Meanwhile, 71% make decisions daily, 61% face daily time pressure, and 70% work more than 40 hours per week. Schedules are regular for 81% and irregular for 19%, associated with refueling outages, unit status and shift rotations.

Shifts and status changes determine the daily rhythm. Operating shifts typically rotate, while refueling outages, unit startup and shutdown and periodic tests may bring temporary overtime and additional coordination. Deliverables are continuous operating records and completed abnormality responses, rather than one-off outputs.

The emphasis is on connecting parameter trends with expected responses: linking readings, trends, procedural steps, expected responses and deviation handling, and immediately reporting to supervisors and taking corrective or shutdown actions under procedures when outcomes exceed expectations.

O*NET's interest code is RC (Realistic, Conventional). Work styles emphasize perseverance, stress tolerance, self-control, achievement orientation, caution, integrity, attention to detail and dependability. Abilities emphasize problem sensitivity, information ordering, oral and written comprehension and expression, deductive reasoning, auditory sensitivity, mathematical reasoning and time sharing. Job Zone 3 (SVP 6.0 to <7.0), with education survey results of 50% high school diplomas or equivalent, 16% college certificates and 15% bachelor's degrees. The daily workflow involves confirming unit status and procedural applicability, reading and comparing parameter trends, performing procedural actions or tests, recording and reviewing, and reporting and escalating abnormalities. Scope statement | This checklist cannot replace nuclear power plant operating procedures, technical specifications, emergency operating procedures, quality assurance systems or operator licensing. Main risks include incorrect parameter trend judgments or delayed responses, control actions deviating from procedures, improper equipment isolation and maintenance permits, incomplete operating records, failed radiation and contamination control, and actions beyond license and role authorization. Controls should be tailored to unit status, facility procedures and regulatory requirements.

Direct answer | Main risks include incorrect interpretation of abnormal signs or delayed responses, control actions deviating from procedures or exceeding license scope, maintenance risks from improper equipment isolation and work permits, incomplete operating records and test data, and emergency direction and communication errors. Controls depend on procedural discipline, periodic testing and supervision, simulator retraining and requalification, clear reporting and escalation chains, and complete operating records.

Evidence scope | Risk items derive from O*NET 51-8011.00 tasks and work contexts: 91% rating accuracy extremely important, 82% reporting extremely serious error consequences, 66% holding extremely high responsibility for others' health and safety, 38% daily radiation exposure, and 61% daily time pressure. They also draw on licensing, retraining and role authorization requirements in China's Provisions on Qualification Management of Civilian Nuclear Facility Operating Personnel, the Nuclear Safety Law's requirements for operating organizations' overall responsibility and personnel training and protection, and US NRC operator licensing and requalification oversight. Controls should be tailored to facilities and jurisdictions.

Shifts, prolonged watch, abnormality handling and handoffs all require sustained attention and procedural discipline. This review did not obtain comparative evidence by seniority or fatigue group and cannot claim newcomers are most likely to miss checks. Control risks through facility guidance, shift and review systems.

Possible consequences | Judgment or operating errors may cause unplanned reactor shutdown, equipment damage or unnecessary personnel exposure. Improper isolation and permits may injure maintenance personnel. Missing records impair event analysis and regulatory tracing. Operation beyond license scope constitutes unauthorized operation subject to legal penalties.

Skill development should begin with supervised learning of facility systems, procedures and technical specifications. After obtaining licensure and role authorization, independently undertake operating shifts, then abnormality handling and emergency direction, and finally operations management, training and procedure improvement. Each step requires training and assessments, operating shift hours, health conditions and facility role authorization. Senior operator licensing typically requires at least two years as an operator and prescribed operating shift hours.

Study reactor physics, thermal hydraulics, electrical systems and instrumentation and control, and radiation protection through guided and simulator training. Supervised learning stage

Boundary note one | Education, training, licensure, facility role authorization and operating shift qualifications are distinct statuses. Licensure does not automatically confer authorization at other facilities; transfers to facilities not specified on the license require a change application and differences training.

Boundary note two | Operating shift hours are an ongoing condition. Nuclear power plant operators must complete at least 400 operating shift hours every 12 months and at least 150 hours every 6 months; role authorization must be withdrawn if these conditions are not met.

Boundary note three | Health conditions and professional conduct are ongoing obligations. Operators must maintain required health conditions and promptly report alcohol, medication or other circumstances that may affect duties. Concealment or false materials affects license applications.

Boundary note four | Operators do not bear all facility responsibilities. Maintenance, radiation protection, quality assurance and regulation belong to different roles and departments. The operating organization bears overall nuclear safety responsibility, and actions beyond license scope constitute unauthorized operation.

After obtaining licensure and role authorization, independently complete routine operating shifts: read and compare parameter trends, perform procedural actions and periodic tests, and record operating data, explaining the bases for readings, actions and review.

Participate in abnormality diagnosis and correction, perform power reductions, shutdowns or isolations and direct shifts under emergency operating procedures, and escalate and report to supervisors when responses exceed expectations.

components.definition_block: Power operators (O*NET-SOC 51-8011.00, Nuclear Power Reactor Operators) operate or control nuclear reactors from nuclear power plant main control rooms: following policies and procedures to protect personnel and the environment; adjusting control rod positions under standard procedures to regulate reactivity, reactor period, coolant temperature or power change rates; monitoring plant-wide system operation and examining instrument readings; recording operating data such as surveillance tests; executing startup and shutdown procedures; diagnosing system or unit abnormalities and recommending or taking corrective action; implementing lockout, tagging and isolation to support maintenance; directing operators under emergency operating procedures; supervising technicians following radiation safety procedures; and participating in authorization for sample collection and testing. components.work_context_block: Work context: main control room operation coexists with authorized facility work. Controlled indoor percentages do not establish that all tasks occur in the main control room. O*NET shows 100% daily face-to-face discussions, 99% daily controlled indoor work, 97% daily telephone use, 88% daily email use and 69% constant contact with others. Accuracy is extremely important to 91%, error consequences extremely serious for 82%, responsibility for others' health and safety extremely high for 66%, and decisions very important to coworkers' or organizational outcomes for 72%. Meanwhile, 38% face daily radiation exposure, 76% wear common protective or safety equipment daily, 71% make decisions daily, and 61% face daily time pressure. Workweeks exceed 40 hours for 70%; schedules are regular for 81% and irregular for 19%.

description.text: Power operators (O*NET 51-8011.00, Nuclear Power Reactor Operators) operate and control reactors from nuclear power plant main control rooms, monitor operating parameters, execute emergency procedures and record operating data. This page explains their tasks, preparation requirements, Chinese and US operator licensing and authorization boundaries, and wage and employment definitions.

subject.name: Power operators
subject.summary: Power operators (O*NET-SOC 51-8011.00, Nuclear Power Reactor Operators) operate or control nuclear reactors from nuclear power plant main control rooms: moving control rods and regulating reactivity and power under standard procedures, monitoring coolant temperature and flow, and starting and stopping equipment; monitoring plant-wide operating parameters, recording operating data and performing periodic tests; determining causes of abnormalities and recommending or taking corrective action; implementing lockout, tagging and isolation to support maintenance; responding to accident conditions under emergency operating procedures; and participating in authorization and supervision of nuclear fuel handling, radiation monitoring and sampling. This page uses only official sources to explain occupational scope, tasks, Chinese and US qualification and authorization boundaries, and wage and employment statistical definitions.
